top_choice_rationale: Anne Carson (P001) remains my first choice on the common criteria. Her voice is recognisable within a few lines, and she keeps finding new forms across books: the essay in Eros the Bittersweet, the verse novel in Autobiography of Red, and the elegy in Nox. In the central books the formal choice carries the feeling, so the form is not ornament. The citation scope is bounded to the original poetry, verse narrative, elegy and essay, with translation named only as part of one practice. It does not claim that work after roughly 2010 equals the core. Reservations remain: part of her effect depends on layout and typography that a committee reading in translation or ordinary editions may see only partly, the corpus rests on a handful of books, and the later books are unverified. I have read no text for this exercise and rely on public knowledge. Cărtărescu (P002) is a close second. His scale, distinctive voice and single imaginative project are serious achievements. I cannot judge his Romanian sentence texture or whether the late novels develop or repeat, so I do not rank him higher or lower on that uncertainty. The gap between the two is small and rests on weighting concentrated formal renewal against large-scale construction. The count of colleagues who favour Carson is not a literary reason. No award (P000) ranks last because both leading proposals offer a substantial, defensible literary case.
